metadata.title: NP-completeness of the initial odd-ear prefix
metadata.description:
The variable-threshold decision problem beta(G)>=t for the maximum initial consecutive odd prefix of an open ear decomposition is NP-complete, even on finite simple 2-vertex-connected graphs with a universal vertex whose deletion leaves a connected bipartite graph. The initial circuit and one-edge ears are counted; the first even ear ends the prefix. This gives a full complexity answer to Sebo's OWR 2014 Question 4 and Benchetrit-Sebo's 2015 Question 3.3. It does not assert P!=NP, fixed-threshold hardness, closed-ear hardness or a theorem about the total number of odd ears.

The six-page note combines the classical factor-critical formulation with an explicit cone identity and a polynomial Set Cover reduction. Complete proofs include all preprocessing branches within the cone subclass, private-element perfect matchings, arbitrary partial blocks and omitted distinguished vertices, the exact loss identity d_i-k(a_i-b_i)=b_i(2k-a_i)>=0, connectivity forcing coverage, explicit polynomial encoding and NP certificates. The key estimate is k(r-s)<=T<k; whole-block optimality is never assumed. Classical structural and Set Cover results are credited as established inputs.

Actual primary sources were checked against alternative formulations: Sharifov's induced perfectly matchable objective permits disconnected selections, Weighted Connected Matching maximizes matching-edge weights rather than all induced edges, and constrained-ear and matroid-join results have different objectives. Bounded primary-source, live-register, public Zenodo and local-state checks on 22 October 2026 authenticated no earlier publication of the full target. This is not exhaustive priority, exclusive firstness or current-openness certification. Catalog 30002726 / OWR-13353-012 and project PR1372 identify one result family; source and dependency DOIs are references only.

The deposit consists of the manuscript PDF and a complete editable source and exact-verification ZIP. Standard-library diagnostics compare 10 actual complete-ear/cone/factor-critical objectives, examine 70 set systems / 194 thresholds and 180 full-size forward matching witnesses, test 142 preprocessing cases and 9454 omission identities, and reject 7 false controls. Finite diagnostics supplement the universal proof and do not certify priority. AI tools were extensively involved in mathematical research, proof development/reconstruction, computational verification, literature investigation, manuscript preparation, editing and adversarial auditing. Alec Kriebel is the named human author. This is an unrefereed preprint without formal independent human peer review, journal acceptance or proof-assistant certification; internal AI audits do not supply those certifications. Authored prose is CC BY 4.0 and authored code is MIT licensed.

metadata.title: NP-completeness of three-terminal shortest-path blocking
metadata.description:
We prove NP-completeness of undirected, unit-traversal-length three-terminal Blocking Shortest Paths: delete a minimum edge set to increase every pairwise terminal distance by at least one. Hardness holds with unit deletion costs and all three original terminal distances equal to three. A direct Vertex Cover reduction also proves NP-completeness when all terminal distances must remain finite, or increase exactly from three to four. The result classifies the undirected triangle question posed by Stefan Krause in 2005. The classical subdivision identity is credited to Poljak (1974), and the related tripartite attachment mechanism to Khachiyan and coauthors (2008). Historical first priority and continued open status through 2026 are not asserted.

This unrefereed research note includes a source and verification archive with the unchanged original proof packet, explicit hash manifests, source-free standard-library Python reproduction, independent adversarial mathematical and computational audits, source-model checks and a bounded priority audit. AI tools were used extensively for construction, verification, adversarial review and writing. Independent AI-agent review is not independent human peer review or journal review; this work has undergone neither. Finite computations supplement the written universal proof and are not formal proof-assistant certification.
